name: magic-lantern
description: Magic Lantern — workspace root. See docs/ for the design doc and the implementation plan.

scripts.dev: pnpm run dev:deps && pnpm --parallel --filter @bureaucromancer/lantern-server --filter @bureaucromancer/lantern-app run dev
scripts.lint: pnpm run lint:es && pnpm run lint:css
scripts.openapi:check: pnpm --filter @bureaucromancer/lantern-server emit-openapi && git ls-files --error-unmatch -- packages/server/openapi.json && git diff --exit-code -- packages/server/openapi.json

scriptsNote: Workspace packages resolve each other through `dist`, so anything that imports one needs `tsc -b` first: `dev:deps` builds the packages the dev servers import (a fresh `pnpm dev` fails without it, and edits to schema, client or react need it re-run), and CI runs `typecheck` — which emits — before `lint`, because the boundary rule classifies an unresolved import as unknown and silently allows it. `typecheck` uses `--force` because `tsc -b` replays no diagnostics for projects it considers up to date. `openapi:check` requires the spec to be tracked before diffing, because a diff compares the tree with the index and a spec that was never committed is in neither; it checks with `git ls-files` rather than marking the file intent-to-add, which would leave an index entry behind that makes `git stash` fail.
devDependenciesNote: Toolchain only; every pin matches StoryEngine's so the two repositories upgrade together, except vitest: 4.1.11, because StoryEngine's 4.1.10 has a published advisory (GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9, path traversal in @vitest/mocker), and StoryEngine should move too. tools/advisory-floors.test.ts holds the lockfile at or above every such floor, so copying StoryEngine's pin back fails a test. `jsdom` is declared here because vitest imports it from its own bundle. `tsx` is here rather than in the server because both the server's watch script and the CLI tests (`node --import tsx`) resolve it from the workspace: Node's type stripping does not remap the `.js` import specifiers this codebase writes. React, Vite, Tailwind and Testing Library live in the packages that use them, never here, because a second copy of React fails as 'Invalid hook call'.
